source_text:
Ἀπεκρίθη
δὲ ὁ Πέτρος λέγων αὐτῷ· «Ἃ προσδοκᾷς λαβεῖν οὐκ ἔχω, ἃ δὲ μὴ προσδοκᾷς λαβεῖν
ἔχω. Ἀργύριον προσδοκᾷς λαβεῖν, ὑγίειάν σοι παρέχω· κρεῖττον γὰρ ὑγίεια σώματος
ἢ ὄλβος ἀμέτρητος. Ὁμο-λογήσω σοι τὴν ἀλήθειαν· "3Ἀργύριον καὶ χρυσίον οὐχ
ὑπάρχει μοι"3. Ὁ Χριστὸς γὰρ παρέδωκεν ἡμῖν λέγων· "3Μὴ κτήσασθε χρυσὸν μηδὲ
ἄργυρον μηδὲ χαλκόν"3. ∆έδωκεν δὲ ἡμῖν ἐξουσίαν λέγων· "3∆αιμόνια ἐκβάλλετε,
ἀσθενοῦντας θεραπεύετε, λεπροὺς καθαρίζετε. ∆ωρεὰν ἐλάβετε, δωρεὰν δότε."3
"3Ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει.» Καὶ κρατήσας «τῆς δεξιᾶς
χειρὸς ἤγειρεν αὐτόν.» Ὁ δοῦλος κρατῶν ἐγείρει, ὁ δεσπότης λόγῳ θεραπεύει· «Οὐ
γάρ ἐστιν δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ.»
7 Ἀλλὰ γὰρ ἰατρείων κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην ἀνοιγομένων, σήμερον βλέπω καὶ
ἕνα τοῖς πᾶσιν ἰατρὸν ἐφεστῶτα Χριστόν. Ὢ καινοτέρου τοῦ θαύματος. ∆ιάφορα
πάθη, ἐν διαφόροις ἰατρείων χωρίοις, ὑπὸ ἑνὸς ἰατροῦ θεραπεύεται. Ἄλλος ἀλλαχοῦ
ἁμαρτίας τραύματι συνεχόμενος πρόσεισιν καὶ παρὰ τῆς νηστείας λαβὼν ἰάσεως
ἔμπλαστρον ἄπεισιν. Ἄλλος ἑτέρωθι σηπεδόνα πορνείας ἀπόζων ἰατικὸν τῆς
δυσωδίας, παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ τῶν ψυχῶν καὶ σωμάτων Χριστοῦ, δι' αὐτῆς ἐκδέχεται
φάρμακον. Ἄλλος πυρετῷ φιλαργυρίας συγκαιόμενος, παρὰ τῆς νηστείας
ἀναψυχούσας τὴν νόσον βοτάνας κομίζεται.
8 Οἶδεν αὕτη καὶ στείρας ἐγκύμονας ἀποφαίνειν συντόμως, καὶ τὴν ἄγονον
μήτραν εὔκαρπον ἄρουραν ἀπεργάζεσθαι, καὶ προφήτας υἱοὺς τῆς ἀσιτίας διδόναι
μισθόν. Τί γὰρ παρὰ τῆς θείας γραφῆς διδασκόμεθα; «Καὶ ἠθύμει Ἅννα», φησίν, «καὶ
ἔκλαιεν καὶ οὐκ ἤσθιεν.» Ἀλλὰ νηστεία τῇ στείρᾳ Σαμουὴλ τὸν προφήτην παρέσχεν.
Εἶδες τῆς νηστείας τὰ δῶρα.
thought_title: Peter heals the lame man; fasting as the universal clinic
orientation: Hesychius is retelling the healing of the lame man at the temple gate by Peter, then turning to fasting as the one physician present in every clinic throughout the world.
pass_a_gloss: Answered [then] Peter saying to him: "What you expect to receive I do not have, but what you do not expect to receive I have. Silver you expect to receive; health to you I provide; for better [is] health of body than wealth immeasurable. I will confess to you the truth: 'Silver and gold [there] is not to me.' For Christ handed over to us, saying: 'Do not acquire gold nor silver nor bronze.' He gave [then] to us authority, saying: 'Demons cast out, [the] sick heal, lepers cleanse. Freely you received, freely give.' 'In the name of Jesus Christ, rise and walk.'" And having grasped [him by] the right hand he raised him. The servant grasping raises, the master by word heals; "For [there] is not [a] servant above his lord." But [then], clinics throughout the inhabited world being opened, today I see also one physician standing over all, Christ. O [of] newer the wonder. Different sufferings, in different places of clinics, by one physician are healed. One [man] elsewhere by a wound of sin being held fast approaches and from fasting having received a plaster of healing departs. Another elsewhere [with] a festering sore of fornication stinking [a] healing [medicine] of the stench, from the physician of souls and bodies Christ, through it receives [as] medicine. Another [with] a fever of love of money being burned up, from fasting cooling herbs for the disease carries away. It knows also barren [women] pregnant to make quickly, and the unfruitful womb [into] a fruitful field to work, and prophets [as] sons of abstinence to give [as] reward. For what from the divine scripture are we taught? "And was despondent Hannah," it says, "and wept and did not eat." But fasting to the barren [woman] Samuel the prophet provided. You saw of fasting the gifts.

choices.why: Keeps the verb παρέχω as 'provide' to match the gift-giving register of the passage, and preserves the dative σοι as 'you'.
ὄλβος is poetic for material prosperity; 'wealth' fits the contrast with bodily health, and ἀμέτρητος is literally 'unmeasured'.

choices.english: with clinics being opened throughout the inhabited world
choices.why: The genitive absolute is rendered as an attendant circumstance; 'clinics' follows the glossary for ἰατρεῖον, and 'inhabited world' keeps the literal sense of οἰκουμένη.
rejected: healing places being opened in the world

choices.english: stinking with the festering sore of fornication
choices.why: ἀπόζων means 'smelling badly', and σηπεδών is a putrefying sore; the rendering keeps the vivid sensory image of moral decay.
rejected: reeking of the rot of fornication
emitting the stench of fornication's decay

choices.english: burning with the fever of love of money
choices.why: συγκαίομαι is 'to be burned up together'; 'burning with the fever' preserves the metaphor of illness as heat, and φιλαργυρία is literally 'love of silver/money'.
rejected: consumed by the fever of greed

choices.why: ἀναψύχω means 'to cool, refresh'; the herbs are the remedy fasting provides, and 'cool the disease' keeps the medical metaphor of fever.

bible_refs.note: Ἀργύριον καὶ χρυσίον οὐχ ὑπάρχει μοι

∆αιμόνια ἐκβάλλετε, ἀσθενοῦντας θεραπεύετε, λεπροὺς καθαρίζετε. ∆ωρεὰν ἐλάβετε, δωρεὰν δότε.
Ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει
Οὐ γάρ ἐστιν δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ

pass_b_english: Peter answered him, “What you expect to receive, I do not have; but what you do not expect to receive, I do have. You expect to receive silver; I provide you with health. For health of body is better than immeasurable wealth. I will tell you the truth: ‘Silver and gold I do not have.’ For Christ handed over to us, saying, ‘Do not acquire gold or silver or copper.’ And he gave us authority, saying, ‘Cast out demons, heal the sick, cleanse lepers. Freely you received, freely give.’ In the name of Jesus Christ, rise and walk.” And taking hold of his right hand, he raised him up. The servant takes hold and raises; the master heals by a word. For a servant is not above his lord.

But now, with clinics being opened throughout the inhabited world, today I see one physician standing over them all: Christ. O what a new wonder! Different diseases, in different places of the clinics, are healed by one physician. One person, afflicted elsewhere by the wound of sin, comes forward, receives from fasting a plaster of healing, and departs. Another, reeking with the decay of fornication, from Christ, the physician of souls and bodies, receives through fasting a medicine for the stench. Another, burning with the fever of love of money, obtains from fasting herbs that cool the disease.

Fasting knows how to make barren women pregnant quickly, to turn the unfruitful womb into a fruitful field, and to give prophets as sons as the reward of abstinence from food. For what are we taught by the divine Scripture? “And Hannah was despondent,” it says, “and she wept and did not eat.” But fasting provided the prophet Samuel to the barren woman. You have seen the gifts of fasting.

problems.quote: receives through fasting a medicine for the stench from Christ
problems.source_quote: παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ τῶν ψυχῶν καὶ σωμάτων Χριστοῦ, δι' αὐτῆς ἐκδέχεται φάρμακον
problems.why: Agency confused: 'παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ... Χριστοῦ' = 'from Christ the physician', 'δι' αὐτῆς' = 'through it [fasting]'. English makes 'through fasting' modify 'from Christ', but Greek has 'from Christ... through fasting'.
problems.fix: from Christ, the physician of souls and bodies, receives through fasting a medicine

problems.quote: For a servant is not above his lord
problems.source_quote: Οὐ γάρ ἐστιν δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ
problems.why: Wrong scripture citation: John 13:16 has 'οὐκ ἔστιν δοῦλος μείζων τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ' ('greater than'), but this matches Matt 10:24/Luke 6:40 'οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον'/'οὐκ ἔστιν δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον'. The citation should be Matthew 10:24 or Luke 6:40, not John 13:16.
problems.ruling: Source ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον matches Matt 10:24, not John 13:16 (μείζων). Wrong scripture citation misleads reader.

problems.quote: O how new is this wonder
problems.why: Wrong degree: 'καινοτέρου' is comparative ('newer/more novel'), not positive ('new'). The exclamation is 'O newer wonder!' or 'O what a novel wonder!'
problems.ruling: καινοτέρου is comparative 'newer/more novel'; 'new' loses comparative degree, changing meaning.

edits.old: receives through fasting a medicine for the stench from Christ, the physician of souls and bodies
edits.new: from Christ, the physician of souls and bodies, receives through fasting a medicine for the stench

edits.old: O how new is this wonder!

fixed: Agency corrected: 'παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ... Χριστοῦ' = 'from Christ the physician', 'δι' αὐτῆς' = 'through it [fasting]'.
Citation corrected: 'Οὐ γάρ ἐστιν δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ' matches Matthew 10:24/Luke 6:40, not John 13:16.
Degree corrected: 'καινοτέρου' is comparative, so 'newer' rather than 'new'.

problems.quote: stinking with the festering sore of fornication
problems.why: σηπεδόνα is 'festering/decay', not specifically 'sore'; ἀπόζων is 'reeking/stinking'
problems.fix: Another, reeking elsewhere with the decay of fornication

problems.why: καινοτέρου is comparative 'newer', but Greek idiom here is exclamatory genitive 'O newness of wonder!' or 'O what a new wonder!'
problems.ruling: 'καινοτέρου...θαύματος' is exclamatory genitive, 'O newness of the wonder!' 'Newer wonder' is nonsensical English.

edits.old: stinking with the festering sore of fornication
edits.new: reeking with the decay of fornication

fixed: Changed 'stinking with the festering sore of fornication' to 'reeking with the decay of fornication': σηπεδόνα means 'decay/festering', not specifically 'sore', and ἀπόζων means 'reeking/stinking'.
Changed 'O what a newer wonder!' to 'O what a new wonder!': the Greek exclamatory genitive καινοτέρου expresses 'O what a new wonder!', not a comparative 'newer'.

last_rejected.quote: receives from fasting a plaster of healing, and departs. Another, reeking with the decay of fornication, from Christ, the physician of souls and bodies, receives through fasting a medicine for the stench.
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἄλλος ἑτέρωθι σηπεδόνα πορνείας ἀπόζων ἰατικὸν τῆς δυσωδίας, παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ τῶν ψυχῶν καὶ σωμάτων Χριστοῦ, δι' αὐτῆς ἐκδέχεται φάρμακον.
last_rejected.why: Source says the second person receives a 'healing [remedy] for the stench' (ἰατικὸν τῆς δυσωδίας), not 'a medicine for the stench'; ἰατικὸν means 'healing/remedy', not 'medicine' (φάρμακον).
last_rejected.fix: receives through fasting a healing remedy for the stench.
last_rejected.ruling: ἰατικὸν τῆς δυσωδίας modifies φάρμακον: 'healing [remedy] for the stench' = 'a medicine for the stench'; meaning unchanged.

last_rejected.why: φιλαργυρία means avarice/greed, not love of money as affection.
last_rejected.ruling: φιλαργυρία (φίλος+ἄργυρος) literally means love of money/avarice; rendering is within normal range.

last_rejected.why: ἀσιτία means fasting/abstinence generally, not specifically 'from food'.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀσιτία (α- + σῖτος) literally means without food; 'abstinence from food' is accurate, not an addition.
